Every state `hs-run ship` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `no_plan_resolved` | No plan could be anchored: none exists, none is `in_progress`, or two are and the resolver refuses to guess between them. The fix is in `plans/` or in the environment — never in a receipt, which is why this is not the same state as a receipt problem. | `references/preflight-checklist.md` |
| `receipt_missing` | A receipt the stage requires was never produced (or resolves outside the plan's own artifacts dir, which is the same thing as absent for a gate that will not read through an escape). Produce it with the tool that owns it; do not hand-write a receipt to clear a gate. | `plannotator-review-gates`, `references/gate-sequence.md` |
| `receipt_invalid` | The receipt is on disk and unusable — unparseable, missing a required field, naming another plan, carrying a failing check, or a verdict the stage does not accept. The envelope carries the gate's own reason verbatim; open that one file and fix what it names. | `plannotator-review-gates`, `references/gate-sequence.md` |
| `needs_architecture_review` | Every receipt is present and the gate still refuses, for a reason that is not a configuration fault: the diff is structural and the review-decision carries no architecture_review.checked. Reachable only on a protected branch, where the gate runs `merge` (which requires review-decision) rather than `push` (which does not). Load docs/system-architecture.md, judge the drift, and re-record the review-decision with --architecture-checked — this is a receipt you can write, not a config file to go edit. | `architectural-constraints`, `docs/system-architecture.md` |
| `policy_broken` | The gate configuration contradicts itself — a `requires:` naming an artifact kind that does not exist, a stage floor switched on but unreadable, or a rule-scan whose own verdict disagrees with its findings. Fix the CONFIGURATION. Chasing this in the receipts is a loop that never goes green. | `references/gate-sequence.md` |
| `ready` | The push-stage gate checked what it requires and found nothing missing. That is the input to the human confirm, never a substitute for it — the gates here are self-approvable, so `ready` is the one moment the discipline depends entirely on the person. | `auto-decision-ledger`, `references/release-notes.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `gates_not_enforced` | The stage policy requires no receipt at all here, so nothing was checked. "Clear" means nobody asked, not that you are covered — the local posture is generate-here, enforce-in-CI, and this state says so out loud instead of letting an empty tree read as a passing one. |
